observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a faceted chrome-and-rust nut lying on its side with its threaded bore facing left, a short threaded shank and a hexagonal bolthead to the right, and a crack across the nut's top facets. East: the same layout (bore left, shank, bolthead right) and the same crack, drawn visibly smaller than south. North: the same parts tipped diagonally, with the bolthead upper-left, the nut lower-right and the bore opening to the right. Crack present on the bolthead/nut.
observed.south.png: Full-resolution south: a rusted, dulled, faceted nut on its side. The round threaded bore faces the viewer-left, a dark crack runs over the upper facets, and a threaded shank leads to a hex bolthead. Warm orange rust rim light, painterly texture, thin dark outline, clean alpha, no shadow.
observed.east.png: Full-resolution east: almost the same picture as south (bore left, crack across the nut, shank, bolthead right), slightly smaller and a little more orange and dulled. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Full-resolution north: the bolt-and-nut tipped at about 45 degrees, bolthead at upper-left, nut at lower-right with its bore opening toward the right edge. Faceted, rusted, a crack on the bolthead. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the candidate is a tiny brown speck, a few pixels across, in the right-hand cell beside the vanilla human. In the normal-play inset it is barely visible next to the human and the rat.
observed.living_reference.png: Living art: an upright, shiny chrome faceted nut with a bolthead on top, joined by a threaded neck. South shows the nut's round bore facing the camera, east shows the bore on the right side, and north shows a plain faceted rear with no bore. Orange rim light, the same painterly style.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the tipped-over body with the nut's bore (the living south's 'front' feature) toward the camera-left. For a corpse lying on its side this is an acceptable front-ish view, but it is nearly the same picture as east.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North is the body tipped diagonally. The bore is visible at the right end of the nut, but this is an inert machined object with no face or eyes, so nothing reads as a face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three are oblique side-on views of the object lying down, not straight overhead.

SAME_SIZE.seen: South is drawn about 15% larger than east, and north's extra height comes from its diagonal pose. The measured 46% spread is mostly pose; the south/east difference is real but modest.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Every facing has the same faceted nut with a bore, threaded shank, hex bolthead, crack and rust palette, all matching the living reference.

SIGNATURE.seen: The large faceted nut with the bolthead joined by a threaded shank is clearly legible in all facings.

ALIEN.seen: A machine-creature; there is no Earth animal to resemble. It reads as an oversized faceted nut and bolt, as the def intends.

DEPARTURES.seen: Line 1: no limbs and no face, a machined nut with a bolthead: present. Line 2: lying tipped on its side, cracked and dulled: present (horizontal or diagonal pose, a visible crack, rust-dulled chrome).

CANON.seen: The card lists no canon Must show lines.

STYLE.seen: Painterly metal with rust texture and a thin dark outline. Not cartoonish, not a photo or a 3D render.

OURS.seen: Derived from the mod's own installed living art; same palette and faceting.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-out on every facing, with no ground, shadow or halo.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: Large nut with a bolthead: yes. Advanced faceted geometry: yes. Oddly shiny: deliberately dulled for the corpse, with some sheen left. Tiny 0.1 size: yes.

SCALE.seen: A speck beside the human in scale.png, consistent with the 'little button' at drawSize 0.1.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell it is about 3 px, a dot by design. The owner asked for button size, so legibility at this zoom is not a meaningful ask.

reply.image_seen: The composite and individual sprites show cracked, tarnished nut-and-bolt bodies lying horizontally in south/east and diagonally in north; the scale panel shows a tiny button-sized object, and the living reference shows an upright, shinier mechanism.

concerns.evidence: At the shared scale, south has a visibly larger nut and bolthead than east. Both bodies lie almost horizontally, so their similar poses do not explain the difference in component size; north's diagonal pose does explain some of its greater height.

The views share a resting orientation but show different projections: south exposes a broader bore opening and larger upper nut surface, while east shows a narrower bore and different facet proportions. They are distinct views rather than duplicate pictures.

Broad silver highlights remain on the nut facets and bolthead, with bright reflective edges in all three views. Rust and darkening occupy the recessed surfaces, consistent with the corpse description's explicit requirement for a dulled, rusted version of the shiny living reference.

request.prompt: A sprite sheet of three views of the same dead Living Bolt, a tiny Rust Cathedral creature of mechanoid flesh, in painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, with a clean dark outline on a transparent background. The body is a large chrome nut with a short shank and a bolthead above it, a machined object with smooth metal surfaces. The creature is spent and stilled: tipped onto its side on the ground, limp, its chrome dulled and streaked with rust-orange, a jagged crack running through the nut. The views are south, east and north, drawn at one identical scale: the nut has the same width in all three, and the bolthead, shank and cracked nut keep the same size and proportions in every view, each centered in its own cell with the same margin around the body. South and east share the same tipped resting pose; east shows the nut and bolthead side by side in profile, and south shows the same parts from the front of the pose with the same dimensions, differing only by viewing angle. North shows the same body from behind with the same nut width and the same crack on the back of the nut. Simple, bold shapes that stay readable at button size.
